subject: Linguistics
title: Pro-Drop Languages
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pro-Drop Languages.

hook.text: In Spanish you can just say 'como'—'I eat'—without ever saying 'yo' (I).

buildup.text: Pro-drop languages allow speakers to omit the subject pronoun because the verb marks it.

discovery.text: Italian, Japanese, and Mandarin are all pro-drop—but for different linguistic reasons.

twist.text: English is non-pro-drop: 'Raining' needs a dummy 'it'—'It is raining'—even though 'it' means nothing.

climax.text: Children in pro-drop languages drop subjects earlier, suggesting they tune into verb morphology fast.

punchline.text: Some languages say more with fewer words.

quiz.question: What is a pro-drop language?
options: One that allows omitting subject pronouns
One with no pronouns at all
